title: Mobility through exercise in shared accommodation managed by care homes and retirement homes
summary:
As people age, their physical abilities may decline, which in turn has a negative impact on their independence and ability to participate in society. For example, getting out of bed or a chair becomes more difficult, or their gait becomes more unsteady. To counteract this, various highly effective forms of exercise have been developed. Unfortunately, residents of supported shared accommodation are particularly at risk, as these targeted programmes are often not available there. 
The Geriatrics Research Department at Robert Bosch Hospital therefore wishes to investigate whether offering targeted exercise programmes in supported shared accommodation is feasible and would be well received. To this end, the training session is first broadcast from Robert Bosch Hospital to the shared accommodation via a large screen. At a later time, a daily support worker from the supported shared accommodation then leads the training session that was previously demonstrated on screen. In addition, residents are given the opportunity to carry out the exercises independently, either on their own or with relatives, using a tablet provided free of charge.
conditions: The study examines the feasibility of a training programme in supported shared accommodation schemes.

interventions.name: The intervention begins with a 12-week tele-based group programme led by a physiotherapist from Robert Bosch Hospital via a large screen in the supported shared accommodation (AbW) settings. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Risk of loss of mobility
Risk of functional impairment
Risk of increased need for care
Motivation and voluntary participation
Exclusion criteria:
Medical reasons for not exercising
Unable to participate in group activities
